$comment: The one type-check project allowed to know a browser exists (#259). Two things are overridden here and
nothing else: `lib` gains `DOM`, `jsx` gains `react-jsx`. Every strictness flag comes from the root config
through `extends`, so the UI tree is not quietly held to a laxer standard than the server tree, and a
tightening landed in the root file tightens this one the same day.
Why this file exists: the root program's include globs are `.ts`-only and it declares no `jsx`, so the
first `.tsx` screen would have been transpiled by `tsx` at run time and never type-checked in CI. Why it is
scoped to one package: the root program's `lib` is ["ES2023"] with no `DOM` precisely so a stray `document`
in packages/contracts or apps/control-plane is a COMPILE error. Adding `DOM` tree-wide would trade that
compiler guarantee for a grep, and that is the trade this issue refuses to make.
Why the three scripts below belong to THIS project and not the root one: `check-ui.ts` and `gen-ui-css.ts`
import this package's modules, and TypeScript follows imports out of an `exclude`d directory. Left in the
root program they drag every `.tsx` screen into a config with no `jsx` and fail with TS6142 (measured on
this tree), and the tempting fix -- `jsx` plus `DOM` in the root file -- is the trade above. So the gate
scripts are checked here, where JSX and DOM exist. The price is stated rather than hidden: inside those
three files a stray `window.` is no longer a compile error. Gate TS0 in scripts/check-ui.ts is the grep that
keeps paying on their behalf, and it is falsified by test like every other gate in this package.
Why not `composite` + `tsc -b`, which would have cost nothing: measured on this tree, a composite
packages/ui refuses `packages/ui/test/source-scan.test.ts` for importing `scripts/ui-source-scan.ts` outside
its rootDir -- TS6059 and TS6307 together. Making that legal means moving a gate's own source into this
package or leaving a file unchecked, and a coverage hole is worse than a grep. So: two explicit
`tsc --noEmit -p` invocations in the `typecheck` script, no emitted artifacts, no build order to get wrong.
`exclude` keeps the negative fixtures out, exactly as the root config does. Those four files must NOT
compile; scripts/check-ui.ts compiles each one standalone and reads the compiler's answer.
Screens under `apps/*` later (the open UI-OD1 shell) are not forbidden by accident: give that app a
tsconfig.json with `jsx`, add one `tsc --noEmit -p apps/<name>` to the `typecheck` script, and
scripts/check-project.ts's typecheck-coverage rule holds the lists in step -- it fails a tracked
`.ts`/`.tsx` that no project claims, a `.tsx` claimed by a project that does not declare `jsx`, a
tsconfig the `typecheck` script never runs, and a `test` glob that matches nothing.
